title: One domain per package
statement: Every Go package under internal and cmd MUST hold only files that the technical records of one domain name, besides the product's shared value types; a package whose files two domains name MUST be split, one package per domain.

title: The code is named as the record names it
statement: A technical record's title MUST be the package-qualified identifier its file declares, such as assure.Verdict, and that identifier MUST be declared in the file the record names; a record whose identifier the file does not declare is not built.

title: Imports follow the domain order
statement: A package of one domain MUST import a package of another domain only along the order: Assuring and Declaring import no other domain; Supplying imports Declaring; Generating imports Declaring and Supplying; Extending imports Declaring and Generating; Building imports Generating; Distributing and Delivering import Building. A cmd package MAY import any domain; shared value types and the standard library belong to no domain.

title: A test names what it proves
statement: Every test function or subtest that proves a test record MUST carry that record's ID in its name, and every test file MUST carry at least one test record's ID; a test file that names no record proves nothing.

title: No source file without a record
statement: Every source file under internal, cmd, scripts and registry MUST be named by a technical record, directly or through a folder the record names; a change that adds a file no record names MUST add its record in the same change or not add the file.

title: A stub is not built
statement: A function that a predicate, handler or service record names MUST read its inputs; a function whose body only returns constants, or only panics, MUST NOT count as built, and assure judge change MUST refuse a change that adds one.

title: A generator does no I/O
statement: A generator MUST NOT read or write files, use the network or start a process. It MUST work only from the context the compiler gives it.

title: A generator reads no clock, environment or randomness
statement: A generator MUST NOT read the clock, the environment or a source of randomness.

title: A generator's output does not depend on map order
statement: A generator MUST return its files, and write their content, in an order that does not depend on the iteration order of a Go map.

title: The library is not a framework
statement: The runtime library MUST expose functions and types only. It MUST NOT scan, discover or register anything by name, struct tag or init(), and MUST NOT call into a service except through a value the service's own code passed it.

title: No reflection, no unsafe
statement: The runtime library MUST NOT import reflect or unsafe; where encoding needs reflection, it MUST go through the standard library at the service's own call.

title: A breaking change is a new major module
statement: The library's API MUST stay compatible within a major version, checked by apidiff in the common registry's CI, and a breaking change MUST ship as a new major module path.

title: One module, released with the common registry
statement: The runtime library MUST be one Go module with one package per concern, tagged and released with the common registry, so one pin names it.

title: Static code lives here
statement: Code that is the same for every declaration MUST live in the runtime library and MUST NOT be emitted by a generator; code that varies with the declaration MUST be generated and MUST NOT be interpreted by the library at run time.

title: One signed compiler holds every generator
statement: STEGO MUST ship as one signed artifact that contains every generator it can run.

title: The compiler runs no generator code it does not contain
statement: The compiler MUST NOT load, download or execute generator code that its signed artifact does not already contain.

title: An adapter reaches only named origins
statement: An adapter that sends a request MUST send it only to an origin its configuration names, over TLS with an explicit CA bundle and no ambient credential, and MUST refuse a response larger than its stated limit.

title: A pulled artifact is verified before use
statement: An adapter MUST check an artifact it pulls against the digest it asked for, or against the trusted signer the registry's ci-pipeline component names, before any other code reads it, and MUST refuse one that differs or that another identity signed.

title: A GitOps adapter writes files and applies nothing
statement: An adapter for a GitOps tool MUST write declarative files that the tool pulls from git, and MUST NOT call the tool's API, hold its credential or apply a resource to a cluster.

title: A published event is a versioned record at a known address
statement: A published event's durable form MUST be a versioned record at a known address: the service repository's .stego/state.yaml, the registry in git, the CI provider's attestation store or an OCI referrer. The command that consumes the event MUST read that record at its next run, and STEGO MUST NOT depend on a relay or a running service to deliver it.

title: Two tenant controls that fail differently
statement: Every generated store method MUST take a tenant of the distinct Tenant type and add the tenant predicate, and every tenant-owned table MUST have row-level security enabled and forced with one policy on the transaction-local tenant setting; a zero tenant MUST be refused before any query, never treated as an empty filter.

title: The tenant setting is transaction-local
statement: The adapter MUST set the tenant with set_config(name, value, true) at the start of every transaction and nothing MAY use a session-scoped SET, so a pooled connection never carries one tenant to the next client.

title: The runtime role owns nothing and bypasses nothing
statement: The database role a service runs as MUST NOT own any table, MUST NOT hold BYPASSRLS, and MUST hold only the privileges the generated code uses; migrations MUST run as the owner role in a separate job.

title: No tenant-less path from a request
statement: A worker or controller that touches more than one tenant MUST iterate tenants and open one transaction per tenant with that tenant set; no code path reachable from a request MAY run without a tenant, and the tenant MUST come from a verified identity claim, never from a client-supplied header or body field.

title: The audit row commits with the change
statement: Every mutation of an audited entity MUST write its audit row in the same transaction as the change, and a denied or failed mutation MUST write its audit row with the outcome in its own short transaction, so there is no record without a change and no change without a record.

title: The audit table is append-only and copied out
statement: The runtime role MUST hold INSERT only on the audit table, a trigger MUST reject UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE, and every audit row MUST also be enqueued in the outbox for the audit sink, keyed by the audit event id, so the sink is idempotent and the service cannot edit its own history.

title: A hash chain over redacted records, anchored outside
statement: Each audit row MUST carry prev_hash and hash over the canonical redacted record, fields declared pii MUST be redacted before hashing and fields declared secret MUST never be stored, and a periodic job MUST publish the chain head and row count to the sink, because a chain alone does not detect truncation.

title: Deny is a decision with a consistency floor
statement: Every authorization check MUST carry a consistency of at least the token stored on the resource row, a deny MUST be a decision and not an error, a list MUST be filtered to the resources the subject may see and an empty list MUST be 200, and the tenant predicate MUST be applied before any authorization filter.

title: System principals are subjects, never a bypass
statement: A worker, controller or relay MUST call the authorization port with its own service-account subject that the schema grants relations to; a bypass flag in a slot or a setting MUST be refused at generation.

title: Relationships are written only through the outbox
statement: A relationship tuple MUST be enqueued in the same transaction as the row it describes and written to the provider by the relay with idempotent touch and delete operations, in order per resource key, and the token the provider returns MUST be stored on the row; a handler MUST NOT write a tuple directly.

title: The idempotency record commits with the write
statement: An inbound idempotency key MUST be recorded in the same transaction as the write it guards, scoped by tenant, principal and key, with the fingerprint of method, path and body and the stored response; a 5xx response MUST NOT be stored, a concurrent duplicate MUST get 409 and a reused key with a different fingerprint MUST get 422, as the IETF Idempotency-Key header draft states.

title: Money is integer minor units with a currency
statement: A money amount MUST be an integer of minor units with an ISO 4217 currency code, a float MUST be refused at checking, and a ledger MUST hold one currency, so a cross-currency move is two transfers through a conversion account.

title: A ledger is append-only and balanced
statement: A transfer and its entries MUST be inserted in one statement that rejects an unbalanced set, posted entries MUST NOT be updated or deleted, a correction MUST be a new transfer that names the one it reverses, a pending transfer MUST be posted or voided by a new row and only once, and a balance MUST be derived from entries after the latest snapshot.

title: Rows are owned by the lock that claimed them
statement: Outbox and job rows MUST be claimed with SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and every handler MUST be idempotent, because the relay can crash after acting and before recording the fact; a session-scoped advisory lock MUST NOT be used, since it is orphaned behind a transaction pooler.

title: A controller holds a lease with a fencing token
statement: One controller instance MUST be active at a time, elected on a lease row whose renewal increments a fencing token, and every write the controller makes MUST carry that token and fail when the lease holds a higher one; on shutdown the holder MUST release the lease and flush its checkpoint. Where the provider behind a write cannot refuse a stale token, takeover MUST fail closed: the controller runs one replica, a lease that expires is not taken over, and an operator restarts the holder.

title: Modes are component sets in one binary
statement: A service MUST be one binary that runs the api, worker and controller modes selected by a repeatable flag, with all as the default, each mode with its own readiness and shutdown sequence; a mode MUST be a named component set and never a fixed bundle.

title: Declared invariants have one known emission
statement: A declared invariant MUST be one of unique in a scope, no overlap on a range, or sum limit under a parent, emitted as a unique index, an exclusion constraint, or a constraint trigger that locks the parent row; a rule with no such emission MUST stay a slot.

title: Authorization covers every exposed operation, or the declaration is refused
statement: When a declaration binds an authorization provider, every entity a collection reads MUST declare a resource type and every operation of every collection MUST name a permission of that type, or public with a reason; checking MUST refuse an entity or an operation left out, naming each, and the emitted router MUST register a route only from the permission table, so a route without a decision cannot exist.
